# qualys_was_application (Resource)

A Qualys WAS web application: the scan target that option profiles, auth
records and scan schedules reference.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "qualys_asset_tag" "was_targets" {
  name = "WAS Targets"
}

resource "qualys_was_auth_record" "storefront_login" {
  name = "Storefront login"

  form_record {
    sub_type  = "STANDARD"
    login_url = "https://shop.example.com/login"
    username  = "scanner"
    password  = var.storefront_scanner_password
  }
}

resource "qualys_was_dns_override" "storefront_staging" {
  name = "Storefront staging DNS"

  mapping {
    host_name  = "shop.example.com"
    ip_address = "10.20.0.5"
  }
}

resource "qualys_was_application" "storefront" {
  name = "Storefront"
  url  = "https://shop.example.com"

  tag_ids         = [qualys_asset_tag.was_targets.id]
  auth_record_ids = [qualys_was_auth_record.storefront_login.id]

  attributes = {
    "Business Unit" = "E-commerce"
    "Cost Center"   = "CC-4471"
  }

  dns_override_ids        = [qualys_was_dns_override.storefront_staging.id]
  default_dns_override_id = qualys_was_dns_override.storefront_staging.id

  cancel_scans_after_hours = 8

  malware_monitoring   = true
  malware_notification = true
}
```

## Tags

`tag_ids` associates the web application with tags from the shared,
subscription-wide tag tree (see `qualys_asset_tag`) — the same tree used to
target VM scans and reports. Each apply sends the full set as an
authoritative replacement, so a tag removed from configuration is
disassociated, not merely left unmanaged.

## Authentication records

`auth_record_ids` associates `qualys_was_auth_record`s with this web
application. Unlike `tag_ids`, a user-supplied example shows this managed
through a separate add/remove call rather than an authoritative replace —
this provider diffs the configured set against state on each apply and
sends only the IDs that were added or removed, including on first creation
(the same example states that creating an auth record never auto-attaches
it to a web application).

## Cancellation, DNS overrides and the `config` landmine

`cancel_scans_at`/`cancel_scans_after_hours` and `default_dns_override_id`
all live under a single `config` element on the wire. A user-supplied "Gap
Review" document, quoting the official Qualys WebApp reference, documents a
genuine API behaviour this provider reproduces faithfully rather than
papering over: **`config` is only sent when at least one of those three
fields is set in your configuration, and if it is sent without a
cancellation field, Qualys removes any existing default-cancellation
setting as a side effect** — including one configured outside Terraform
(e.g. in the Qualys UI). If you set `default_dns_override_id` and want to
keep an existing cancellation setting, set `cancel_scans_at` or
`cancel_scans_after_hours` explicitly too; leaving all three unset avoids
sending `config` at all, which the same source confirms leaves the existing
setting untouched.

`dns_override_ids` is a separate collection from `default_dns_override_id`
— which DNS overrides are available to this web application, versus which
one is used by default. Confirmed as `dnsOverrides`, sent as a full
authoritative replacement (the "set" idiom) on every apply.

## Files: Swagger/OpenAPI and Postman

`swagger_file` and `postman_collection` are mutually exclusive file uploads
describing this web application's API surface, confirmed against the
official Qualys reference. Both take base64-encoded content — pass
Terraform's `filebase64()` rather than raw text:

```terraform
resource "qualys_was_application" "partner_api" {
  name = "Partner API"
  url  = "https://api.example.com"

  swagger_file {
    name           = "openapi.yml"
    content_base64 = filebase64("${path.module}/openapi.yml")
  }
}
```

Qualys documents a maximum size of 5MB and Swagger/OpenAPI 2.0/3.0 (YAML or
XML); Postman collections v2.0.0/v2.1.0. Neither is read back on `terraform
plan` (no confirmed read shape exists for either), so drift in the uploaded
file content itself is not detected — only whether the block is present at
all.

## Malware monitoring

`malware_monitoring`/`malware_notification` are confirmed flat booleans.
Malware *scheduling* (a recurring malware scan, distinct from vulnerability
scan schedules) is deliberately not modelled: the same source that
confirmed the flags above states its exact recurrence structure "should be
modelled from the corresponding WebApp API examples/XSD rather than
inferred" — an open gap pending that evidence.

## Crawling scripts (read-only)

`crawling_scripts` surfaces Selenium scripts already attached to this web
application (e.g. via the Qualys UI). This provider does not support
creating or updating them — no example for that direction was supplied —
only reading them back for visibility.

## Schema

### Required

- **name** (String) Web application name.
- **url** (String) The application's base URL.

### Optional

- **id** (String) The ID of this resource.
- **tag_ids** (Set of String) Asset tag IDs (see `qualys_asset_tag`) associated with this web application. Tags are the cross-module targeting primitive shared with VMDR and AssetView; a WAS scan schedule can target web applications by tag.
- **auth_record_ids** (Set of String) IDs of `qualys_was_auth_record`s to associate with this web application.
- **attributes** (Map of String) Custom key/value attributes. Sent as a full authoritative replacement on every apply.
- **cancel_scans_at** (String) Absolute RFC3339 time to cancel scans. Conflicts with `cancel_scans_after_hours`. See the note on the `config` landmine.
- **cancel_scans_after_hours** (Number) Cancel scans this many hours after they start. Conflicts with `cancel_scans_at`.
- **default_dns_override_id** (String) ID of the `qualys_was_dns_override` used by default. Should also appear in `dns_override_ids`.
- **dns_override_ids** (Set of String) IDs of `qualys_was_dns_override`s associated with this web application. Sent as a full authoritative replacement.
- **swagger_file** (Block List, Max: 1) A Swagger/OpenAPI definition. Conflicts with `postman_collection`.
  - **name** (String)
  - **content_base64** (String, Sensitive) Base64-encoded file content.
- **postman_collection** (Block List, Max: 1) A Postman collection. Conflicts with `swagger_file`.
  - **collection** (Block List, Max: 1, Required within block) `{name, content_base64}`.
  - **environment_variable** (Block List, Max: 1) `{name, content_base64}`.
  - **global_variable** (Block List, Max: 1) `{name, content_base64}`.
- **malware_monitoring** (Boolean) Enable malware monitoring.
- **malware_notification** (Boolean) Email notification on malware detection.

### Read-Only

- **created** (String)
- **crawling_scripts** (Block List) Selenium crawling scripts already attached to this web application.
  - **id** / **name** / **data** (String)
  - **requires_authentication** (Boolean)
  - **starting_url** (String)
  - **starting_url_regex** (Boolean)

## Import

Web applications are imported by their numeric Qualys ID.

```shell
terraform import qualys_was_application.storefront 12345678
```
